name: Geography
theme: world geography: countries and their capitals, borders and coastlines, rivers, mountains and deserts, cities, islands, and the way places relate to one another on the map
angles: capitals people routinely get wrong because the largest city is a different one
which countries share a border, and the odd exclave or enclave
rivers and what they pass through on the way to the sea
the highest, deepest, driest or longest, and which country it actually sits in
flags, and what a specific element on one stands for
the official language of a country that most people would guess wrong
former names of countries and cities, and roughly when they changed
islands, who governs them and how far they sit from the country that does
time zones, the date line, and countries that sprawl across several
mountain ranges and the countries they divide
lakes and seas that are not what their name says they are
landlocked countries, and the two that are landlocked twice over
cities that straddle two continents, a river or a border
landmarks and the specific country or region they belong to
what people from a place are called, and where a demonym comes from
avoid: live territorial disputes, population and GDP figures that shift year to year, questions that need a map open in front of you, cases where both an old name and a current name would reasonably be right, and capitals of small or remote countries most players have never heard of

easy: In which country is the Eiffel Tower? -> France
What is the longest river in Africa? -> Nile
Which ocean lies between Europe and North America? -> Atlantic
medium: What is the capital of Australia? -> Canberra
In which country is the Atacama Desert? -> Chile
Which river flows through Baghdad? -> Tigris
hard: What is the capital of the Canadian province of British Columbia? -> Victoria
Which country has the most time zones, counting overseas territories? -> France
Lake Titicaca sits on the border of Peru and which other country? -> Bolivia
